title: Podcast Clip Editing Masterclass - Extract Viral Moments

transcript.text: Today I'm going to show you exactly how to take a three hour podcast and extract the most viral clip possible. This is the skill that makes editors six figures.
Step one is listening to the entire podcast. Not skimming, listening. You're looking for moments that make you feel something. Shock, laughter, inspiration, outrage.
The perfect clip has three elements: a strong hook in the first two seconds, a build that keeps attention, and a payoff that makes people share.
When you find the moment, mark the timestamp. Then go back ten seconds before it and five seconds after. That's your raw clip.
The editing technique I use is called the Sandwich Method. Start with the most shocking part, then context, then the full moment with emotional build.
For the hook, you can either start with the punchline cold, or use a text overlay that teases what's coming. Both work, but cold punchlines convert better.
Zoom technique for podcast clips: slow zoom during the setup, then a quick zoom on the key moment. The contrast between slow and fast creates drama.
Cut out every pause longer than half a second. Every um, every stumble. Podcast audio is slow by nature, your job is to make it fast.
Text on screen should highlight the key phrase. Not everything they say, just the one line that matters. Make it big, centered, impossible to miss.
Background music should be subtle. A low tension bed during the build, then drop it out for the punchline. Silence after a big moment is powerful.
The ideal podcast clip is thirty to sixty seconds. Long enough to tell the story, short enough to maintain retention throughout.
End with a cliffhanger or a loop. Never end with a conclusion. Leave them wanting more so they watch again or check out the full episode.
Color correction for podcasts: match the lighting of the original, boost contrast slightly, warm up skin tones. Make the speaker look their best.
Aspect ratio is always nine sixteen for short form. Crop to focus on the speaker's face. If there are two people, alternate between them.

key_techniques: Listen to entire podcast for emotional moments
Sandwich Method: punchline → context → full moment
Start clip 10 seconds before the moment
Slow zoom during setup, quick zoom on key moment
Text overlay on key phrase only
Subtle background music, drop for punchline
